newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-DEPLETED AJAX HOPE TO LIFT GLOOM AGAINST AUXERRE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DEPLETED AJAX HOPE TO LIFT GLOOM AGAINST AUXERRE.

text.p: Depleted by injury, four times European champions Ajax Amsterdam hope they can limp through Wednesday's Champions' League group A match against French title-holders Auxerre and take at least the one point that will guarantee a quarter-final berth.
As their league form goes from bad to worse, extinguishing any realistic hope of a 27th domestic title, Ajax are left chasing a third consecutive European Cup final.
But they must shake off some indifferent league form and recreate the style and concentration that has brought them three wins out of four group A matches.

Buoyed by back-to-back wins against Europe's whipping boys Glasgow Rangers, the Dutch champions will take heart from a convincing 1-0 win in Auxerre in September but will not want to dwell on a home defeat by Grasshopper Zurich, their main rivals to head group A.
That rare European reverse came at a time when Ajax were struggling to find shape, rhythm and form in the Dutch league.
They then strung together a 10-match unbeaten run, but a lethargic 2-2 draw with Fortuna Sittard and Saturday's 2-0 defeat at NAC have plunged the club back into despair.

"We're at the bottom of a crater," said Frank de Boer after Saturday's game, Ajax's third league reverse this season. Ajax have already dropped 21 league points in 16 games, against 19 for the whole of last season's successful title defence.
Injuries and loss of confidence are at the heart of Ajax's uncharacteristic slump.

While internationals Marc Overmars and Patrick Kluivert have recently returned after lengthy lay-offs, Richard Witschge and Peter Hoekstra, both of whom excelled for the Dutch in Euro '96, are long-term casualties and skipper Danny Blind, a mainstay at the heart of the defence, is sidelined until the New Year.

Jari Litmanen, Ajax's most prolific scorer in European competition is also injured, while Winston Bogarde and Arnold Scholten, who scored his first goal in 35 European games against Rangers in Glasgow, are also doubtful starters.
Kiki Musampa, another of the Ajax youngsters thrust prematurely into the first team, faces a late fitness test.

Portuguese striker Dani, who scored twice on his European debut against Rangers but was then dropped, is likely to be recalled in midfield, with Overmars and Nigerian Tijani Babangida supplying the ammunition for Kluivert.
Ajax's problems this year are highlighted by the fact that Kluivert, who has missed more than half the league programme, is the club's top league scorer with just three goals.
Brazilian defender Santos, a World Cup winner with his country but out of favour with coach Louis van Gaal, is suspended after two yellow cards earlier in the group.

Van Gaal, concerned about Santos' failure to fit into the Ajax style, dropped him from the NAC game, saying that the Brazilian was cramping Ajax's fluid style, playing the ball too slowly out of defence and often behind the advancing midfield.

Auxerrre are also depleted by injuries and will start without international midfielder Sabri Lamouchi, young striker Thomas Deniaud, Australian defender Ned Zelic plus strikers Antoine Sibierski and Lilian Laslandes.
To add to their woes, the Burgundy team with also be without suspended international Alain Goma.
Teams:

Ajax (from) - Edwin van der Sar, John Veldman, Frank de Boer, Arnold Scholten, Mario Melchiot, Winston Bogarde; Nordin Wooter, Ronald de Boer, Tijani Babangida, Marc Overmars, Martijn Reuser; Patrick Kluivert, Kiki Musampa, Dani.

Auxerre (probable) - 1-Lionel Charbonnier, 12-Tarbio West, 13-Frederic Danjou, 4-Franck Silvestre, 3-Franck Rabarivoiny, 14-Christian Henna, 6-Philippe Violeau, 8-Moussa Saib, 15-Abdelhafid Tasfaout, 17-Steve Marlet, 11-Bernard Diomede.
